clue.text: Football club's drawn in controlled Eastern country

indicators.note: the club's letters have pulled the next word inside them, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club
to run a business is to control it; past tense
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A football club has been signed up by a tightly run country in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the club has drawn the past tense of run inside it, then Eastern follows.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a European nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Blue movie's first three characters formerly your partners

indicators.note: only the opening three characters of the word are kept, the rest discarded

blocks.note: a movie is a film; its opening letters
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: An adult film: a viewer reads its opening credits, the actors who used to be your partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue movie' runs together as one phrase in the surface, but Blue alone is the definition. 'Partners' is the join: the two pieces are paired.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of obscene or smutty matches filthy, as in a blue joke.

clue.text: A burger roll with caper richness

blocks.note: taken as written
a burger is served in a bun
to caper is to skip or dance about

explanation.surface: A burger roll garnished with capers tastes rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like the pickled flower bud from the menu, but it is the verb for frolicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means plenty or a great quantity, which is a kind of richness.

clue.text: Gather stores I'm organising should be special objects

indicators.note: organising things means putting them in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to collect is to gather
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says that when gathering stock, the things being put in order should be special.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectors' items are pieces prized by collectors for their rarity, making them special objects.

clue.text: Is mum going after cleaner power?

indicators.note: going after says the later words are placed behind the cleaner in the final order

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaning lady
taken as written
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a mother taking a job after the cleaner is a power grab.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning lady; the clue order is reversed, with the cleaner placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal magnetism, a form of power over other people.

clue.text: Current head of Telegraph will uphold hard clue

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept
in a down answer, holding something up means sitting beneath it, so these pieces go below the next

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
in means fashionable or current
the first letter of the newspaper's name

explanation.surface: The current editor of the Telegraph will stand by a difficult clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The hard letter sits on top of the others because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a small suggestion pointing towards an answer, just as a clue is.

clue.text: Pets must be under control - verbally come down hard

indicators.note: verbally means said in speech, so the phrase is judged by how it sounds rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to rein is to keep under control, and cats and dogs are typical pets

explanation.surface: An owner insists that household animals must be disciplined, and harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rein (control with reins) and rain sound the same, so an order to control the pets becomes the idiom for a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: To rain cats and dogs is an idiom for heavy rainfall, so the weather comes down hard.

clue.text: Pledge 20 shillings on top

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top means placed above the other piece, so first in the reading

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for shillings, the old British coin
the answer to 20 across means clothes, which are also called wear

explanation.surface: Someone promises to pay twenty shillings, a pound in old money, as a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is a cross-reference: the 20 across answer, a set of clothes, gives a synonym. Shillings are old British coins, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to promise solemnly, the same act as pledging.

clue.text: Cure's revamped Tainted Love has broken through

indicators.note: something revamped has been remade, so the letters are reworked into a new order
breaking through means forcing a way inside, so this piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A news item: the Cure, the British rock band, have done a revamped version of the song Tainted Love, which has broken through.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cure is a band and Tainted Love a hit song; the 's means 'is', and Cure itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts a poison, so it is a cure.

clue.text: In short, it'll get you an F in music

definitions.text: In short, it'll get you an F in music

blocks.note: surface reading: a bad grade, an F, earned in a music exam
setter's reading: an F in a score is the abbreviation of forte, so the answer is what that letter stands for in shorthand

explanation.surface: A warning to a slacking music student about what will earn a failing grade.
explanation.walkthrough: F looks like a failing grade; in a musical score it is short for forte, an instruction to play at high volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Forte is the Italian direction to play with great volume, so an F in sheet music means play this way.

clue.text: Birdbrain CID entrapped concealing affair

indicators.note: the run of words is concealing the solution inside its letters, spanning the word breaks

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A dim-witted detective from the CID was trapped while covering up a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives; here it simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean an event or occurrence, which is what an incident is.

clue.text: Pine product with penetrating note or scent

indicators.note: to penetrate something is to go into it, so this piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: a pine tree produces cones
to log is to note down in a record

explanation.surface: An air freshener made from pine has a sharp note of perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a perfumer's note, but it is the verb meaning to record.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a light perfume, a type of scent.

clue.text: That man would become bigger shown over electronic green screen

indicators.note: spread over the letter so that it is covered, meaning the word for become bigger wraps around it

blocks.note: he'd is the contraction of he would
to grow is to become bigger
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A man would grow larger when shown in front of a green screen used for electronic special effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green screen' suggests film studio effects; here it is a barrier of living plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a line of bushes along a field, so it forms a leafy barrier that screens the view.

clue.text: Marked one Republican down as nervous

indicators.note: down here means short of, so one of the letters is lost from the word

blocks.note: marked by a scar
R is the abbreviation for Republican; only one of the two is taken away

explanation.surface: A Republican was marked down by the voters as nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for marked has two Rs; losing just one leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scared means feeling fear, and a nervous person is fearful or apprehensive.

clue.text: Give in, troops - they're barbarians!

blocks.note: to cave in is to give in
soldiers are often called men

explanation.surface: A commander urges soldiers to surrender because the enemy are savages.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavemen are primitive people, and the word is used loosely for uncivilised brutes.

clue.text: Run for the public houses?

blocks.note: surface reading: a dash to the pubs, a British word for bars
setter's reading: an organisation that manages stately homes on behalf of the public

explanation.surface: A thirsty crowd makes a dash for the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Public houses are pubs, but read literally they are houses for the public; the National Trust is the British charity that runs historic houses open to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Trust is a British charity that owns and operates country houses which the public can visit.

clue.text: United Nations left touring Conservative bored

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for left wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
to exit is to leave
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A UN delegate walked out from a tour with a Conservative politician because it was dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unexcited feels no enthusiasm, the state of being bored.

clue.text: Disaster from splitting up playmaker's parts

indicators.note: the long compound word is broken into its two component parts, each then replaced by a synonym

blocks.note: the first part of the word; to act is to play a part
the second part: the Maker is God, and the possessive turns into 'of' placed in front

explanation.surface: A disaster comes from splitting a team's playmaker from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Playmaker splits into play and maker; the maker's play becomes the play of the Maker, God.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of God is a natural catastrophe beyond human control, such as a flood, so a disaster.

clue.text: What's in store when everything's ordered to go?

definitions.text: What's in store when everything's ordered to go?

blocks.clueFragment: What's in store when everything's ordered to go?
blocks.note: surface reading: what the future holds when a command to leave is given

blocks.clueFragment: What's in store when everything's ordered to go?
blocks.note: setter's reading: an event in a shop where all the stock must be got rid of

explanation.surface: A worried question about what happens once everyone is ordered out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In store' sounds like 'in the future' but means inside a shop; 'ordered to go' is the stock that must be sold off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop holds this event to sell off its remaining stock cheaply, often before closing or refitting.

clue.text: Cheer breaks out by Duck & Parrot again

indicators.note: something that breaks out is broken apart, so these letters escape their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, which looks like O; by means next to

explanation.surface: Applause erupts for a duck and a parrot, perhaps a comedy double act.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batsman's score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or echo, so to parrot again is to re-echo.

clue.text: Blooming strong team

blocks.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
fit means in good physical shape

explanation.surface: Someone praises a flourishing, powerful sports side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British oath or a word of praise, but it means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is an informal word for a group of people working together, such as a team or band.

clue.text: Heartless toy boy, former champion

indicators.note: without a heart, the middle letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written, then its middle letter is dropped
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A cruel toy boy who was once a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' reads as one phrase for a young lover, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was the undisputed world heavyweight boxing champion in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Leading hospital one's ringing in pain

indicators.note: ringing means forming a ring around something, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to head is to lead, as in the head of a column
an ace is the one in a pack of cards
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone from the top hospital rings up to say they are in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is': the one is ringing the hospital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is a pain in the head, and is also used loosely for any trouble or nuisance.

clue.text: Boyfriend from cockney area, as we can hear

indicators.note: hearing it means judging the word by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: Bow is a district in London's East End, the heart of cockney territory

explanation.surface: A girlfriend's boyfriend hails from London's East End, judging by his accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London; a true cockney is said to be born within the sound of Bow Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male admirer or boyfriend.

clue.text: Power gauge in fuel tank with space for nothing

indicators.note: a gap takes the place of the round symbol for nothing, so that letter is taken out and a break left

blocks.note: a gasometer is a large tank for storing gas
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: A device inside a fuel tank measures power, leaving space for nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the O from the big gas tank and putting a space in its place turns one word into two.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter measures how much gas, a power supply for a home, has been used.

clue.text: Some recite opaquely, coming over as this?

definitions.text: Some recite opaquely, coming over as this?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run inside them
coming over suggests turning over, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Reciting verse obscurely makes you sound like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: reciting something opaquely can come across as poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure, high-flown delivery of a recital can seem like verse, so the speaker comes across as poetic.

clue.text: One's history is around reforms

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are given a new shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old reformer's past is surrounded by new changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'One's history' as 'one who is history': a person who belongs to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a dinosaur is an outdated person, one whose time has passed and who is therefore history.

clue.text: Familiar with American edition, took 50 per cent off

indicators.note: half of the word is taken off, leaving only its first two letters

blocks.note: US stands for United States, hence American
ED is the abbreviation for edition
taken as written before losing its back half

explanation.surface: An American edition was knocked down by half price.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used to something is to be accustomed to it, the same idiom as being familiar with it.
